frequency_question: How often do central bank principals implement an incremental or secondary reserve requirement instrument when excess liquidity conditions arise?
membership_rule: Includes any formal deployment of a secondary, incremental, or special reserve ratio tool by a major emerging market central bank to manage banking system liquidity surpluses. Excludes standard statutory reserve ratio changes that apply permanently.

cases.name: People's Bank of China RRR targeted hikes
Central Bank of Sri Lanka statutory reserve requirement variations
National Bank of Poland supplementary reserve ratio deployment

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 8 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.6x)
coverage_note: 8 named episodes representing the core emerging market central bank demographic utilizing targeted reserve tools.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier economies with non-standard monetary frameworks.
skeleton: Major central banks encountering specific liquidity surges: 8 distinct episodes identified across emerging markets where principals possessed the institutional intent and mandate to deploy temporary reserve ratio tools over the past three decades, resulting in 6 successful deployments of targeted incremental ratios.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 8 relevant historical episodes
validity_reason: Central banking toolkits for liquidity management evolve slowly over decades unless foundational monetary regimes are rewritten.
